text: nature involves something that happens naturally while science has to be triggered by people
llm_text: I mean that nature is the raw reality — the world, events and experiences themselves — while science is a human method for modeling and explaining that reality. Science is brilliant at mechanisms and repeatable facts (how the heart pumps, how cells divide, how stars form), but it relies on measurement, testing and reproducibility. That leaves out or struggles with subjective things (consciousness, qualia), questions of meaning and purpose, and singular or spiritual claims (the soul, miracles) that aren’t easily subjected to repeatable experiments. So science and nature look at the same things from different angles: one is what is, the other is our tool to make sense of it — very powerful, but not necessarily the whole story.
